title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (the 'équation des lacets' series, sequel to the Longue Marche). Notation, partly inferred from the neighbouring pages:
- 𝔖^{+1} (𝔖^+) is the profinite completion of SL2(Z), the amalgam Z/4 *_{Z/2} Z/6. Its generators are σ (order 4) and ρ (order 6), with ρ^3 = σ^2 = -1 central.
- 𝔖 is an extension of 𝔖^{+1} by an involution τ that inverts ρ and σ, i.e. a GL2-type extension.
- π_0 ⊂ π^ ⊂ 𝔖^{+1} are the free profinite 'Γ(2)-type' subgroups. π^ is generated by the cusp loops l_0, l_1, l_∞, and 𝔖^+/π ≅ S_3.
- 𝔖^+/π_0 is the dicyclic group of order 12. Its presentation is (31): ρ^6 = σ^4 = 1, ρ^3 = σ^2, σρσ^{-1} = ρ^{-1}. It is a central extension (32) of S_3 by μ = {±1}.
- On the previous page Grothendieck showed that the automorphisms of this extension inducing the identity on S_3 and on μ form Z/2. Its generator is Θ(x) = sg(x)·x, so Θ(ρ) = ρ and Θ(σ) = -σ.

This page, step by step.

(35) Comparing with formulas (20): an element u of M (his candidate Galois/GT-type group acting on 𝔖^+) induces on 𝔖^{+1}/π_0 the map Θ^{ε_2(u)}. Here ε_2 is the mod-4 sign of the multiplier, Ẑ* → (Z/4)* = ±1.

(35 bis) Equivalently, the commutator in the semidirect product satisfies [u̇, σ̇] = u̇(σ̇)σ̇^{-1} = ε_2(u) in 𝔖/π_0. The left margin generalises this to [u̇, ẋ] = sg(x) for x ∈ 𝔖^{+1} (when ε_2(u) = -1).

(36) He defines Z_{ρ,σ} as the set of u ∈ Aut(𝔖^{+1}) such that:
- u(L_ρ) is conjugate to L_ρ;
- u(L_σ) is 𝔖^{+1}-conjugate to L_σ;
- u(L_0) = L_0.
Here L_ρ and L_σ are the finite cyclic 'elliptic inertia' subgroups and L_0 is the procyclic cusp subgroup generated by ε_0. In modern terms these are automorphisms of π_1(M_{1,1}) respecting the elliptic and cuspidal inertia, with the cusp subgroup normalised exactly.

(37) For u ∈ Z one gets:
- u(ρ) is 𝔖-conjugate to ρ^{ε'};
- u(σ) is 𝔖-conjugate to σ^{ε} = εσ;
- u(ε_0) = ε_0^λ with λ ∈ Ẑ*.
The signs and λ are well defined because Ẑ → 𝔖, 1 ↦ ε_0, is injective, and because ρ is not 𝔖^{+1}-conjugate to ρ^{-1} (nor σ to σ^{-1}). The latter is visible on the abelianisation Z/12 of SL2(Z)^.

Main claim: such a u comes from M_{0,3}^~, i.e. from the group of automorphisms of the profinite π_1 of P^1 - {0,1,∞} with its symmetries. By 'the proposition' it suffices to show that u stabilises π^ = ⟨l_0, l_1, l_∞⟩. The proof:
1. u(l_0) = l_0^λ.
2. l_1 = int(ρ)(l_0), so u(l_1) = (u∘int ρ)(l_0) = int(f)int(ρ^{ε'})(u(l_0)) with f ∈ 𝔖^{+1}. This lies in π^ because π^ is normal.
3. u(-1) = -1, since -1 is the unique nontrivial central element. With l_∞ = -(l_1 l_0)^{-1} this gives u(l_∞) = -u(l_0)^{-1}u(l_1)^{-1} ∈ π.
The last line ('if we identify u with an element of M_{0,3}^~, it is in fact…') is cut off. The next page finishes it: Z^!_{ρ,σ} ≅ M^![0] = M^{!~}_{0,3}[0], with explicit formulas (38)–(39) and the corollary Γ_{ρ,σ} ≅ Γ^~_Q.

Purpose: to characterise Grothendieck's 'Teichmüller-type' Galois substitute Γ^~_Q purely as inertia-preserving automorphisms of profinite SL2(Z) = π_1(M_{1,1}). This identifies the M_{1,1} description with the M_{0,3} description (Legendre/Γ(2) level structure, S_3 symmetry).
errors: Labels of the signs look swapped relative to the next page. In (37) ε' goes with ρ and ε with σ. Formulas (38)–(39) give u(σ) = ε_2·int(β)σ, so ε (for σ) = ε_2(μ), and u(ρ) = int(α)ρ with ε_τ(α) = ε_3(μ), so ε' (for ρ) = ε_3. The next page's proposition states ε = ε_3(μ), ε' = ε_2(μ); one of the two is mislabelled.
Minor notation slip: the last line writes u(l_∞) ∈ π instead of π^.
The step u(-1) = -1 is asserted without comment. It is correct because ±1 is the centre of SL2(Z)^ and -1 its only nontrivial central element of order 2.
'u(L_ρ) conjugué' does not say in which group; (37) uses 𝔖-conjugacy. The extended group 𝔖 is needed because ρ and ρ^{-1} are only conjugate there.
Gap: the stabilisation proof only shows u(π^) ⊂ π^. Equality follows by applying the same argument to u^{-1}, which also lies in Z; not stated.

ideas.what: Profinite SL2(Z) as Z/4 *_{Z/2} Z/6, with the free Γ(2)-type normal subgroup and dicyclic quotient of order 12; Θ = sign twist as the unique nontrivial automorphism of the extension over S_3.
ideas.modern_name: π_1^orb(M_{1,1}) = SL2(Z)^ and its level-2 (Legendre) cover
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme / Longue Marche discuss M_{1,1} and SL2(Z)^ in general terms

ideas.what: Group Z_{ρ,σ} of automorphisms of SL2(Z)^ preserving the conjugacy classes of the elliptic inertia subgroups (orders 4 and 6) and normalising exactly the cusp subgroup, with multiplier λ ∈ Ẑ* and signs ε, ε'.
ideas.modern_name: inertia-preserving (♯ / 'cuspidal and elliptic') automorphism group of π_1(M_{1,1})
ideas.usually_credited_to: Nakamura; Lochak–Nakamura–Schneps (1997) for GT via M_{1,1}; Hoshi–Mochizuki for Out^C-type groups

ideas.what: Proof that any u ∈ Z stabilises the free subgroup π^ = ⟨l_0, l_1, l_∞⟩, hence comes from automorphisms of π_1(P^1 - {0,1,∞}) with S_3-symmetry (M_{0,3}^~). This yields the comparison Z_{ρ,σ} ≅ M^![0] and Γ_{ρ,σ} ≅ Γ^~_Q (next page).
ideas.modern_name: comparison of inertia-preserving automorphisms of π_1(M_{1,1}) and π_1(M_{0,3}) via the Legendre cover

ideas.what: Mod-4 and mod-3 signs ε_2, ε_3 of the cyclotomic multiplier governing the action on the elliptic generators σ, ρ (u(σ) ~ ε_2·σ).
ideas.modern_name: action of Galois/GT on the elliptic inertia of M_{1,1} via χ mod 4 and χ mod 3

missed.claim: Grothendieck proves that automorphisms of profinite SL2(Z) preserving the elliptic inertia classes (up to the sign twist) and the cusp subgroup automatically preserve the level-2 free subgroup. They therefore coincide with the S_3-equivariant 'M_{0,3}^~' automorphisms, giving his group Γ^~_Q a purely M_{1,1}-theoretic description. Comparable M_{1,1} characterisations of GT-type groups appear later (Lochak–Nakamura–Schneps 1997), but this exact construction does not seem to be credited to him.
missed.quote: Je dis qu'un tel u provient de M_{0,3}^~ — il suffit, en vertu de la proposition, que u stabilise π^, qui est engendré par l_0, l_1, l_∞.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical: shows Grothendieck himself worked out an M_{1,1}/SL2(Z)^ model of his Galois-substitute group (the 'one-dimensional' level of the Teichmüller tower). Mathematically the argument is short; the novelty is mostly attribution.

deep.surprise_reason: A clean, finished identification of inertia-preserving automorphisms of SL2(Z)^ with Grothendieck's M_{0,3}^~ group, part of an unpublished construction of Γ^~_Q. The argument itself is elementary, and closely related results exist in the later GT/M_{1,1} literature, so it is a notable unpublished detail rather than a surprise.
transcription_corrections: The number 594 at the top is Grothendieck's own pagination; 580 at the bottom is the archive page.
(35 bis): the second line 'u̇(σ̇)σ̇^{-1}' is the expansion of the commutator [u̇, σ̇], written under it; the value ε_2(u) is in 𝔖/π_0.
(36): read 'u(L_ρ) 𝔖-conjugué à L_ρ' (a correction is overwritten there), 'u(L_σ) 𝔖^{+1}-conj. à L_σ', 'u(L_0) = L_0'. The insertion above 'définition' appears to refer to 𝔖^{+1}.
(37): the exponent in u(ε_0) = ε_0^λ is λ (later called μ); 'σ^ε (= εσ)'.
'car 𝔖^ le fait' is likely 'car π^ est normal dans 𝔖^' or similar; the sense is that int(f)ρ^{ε'} normalises π^ because π^ is normal.
Left oblique margin: roughly 'On a ici [u̇, ẋ] = sg(x) dans 𝔖^{+1}/π_0 (u ∈ M, x ∈ 𝔖^{+1}) (c'est la fonction sg…)', generalising (35 bis).
